The Tribunal Chamber hums with ritual energy, concentric rings of seating rising around the central witness platform. Above, the Codex manifests as a shimmering lattice of light and law, recording every word, every heartbeat, every fluctuation in spiritual resonance. You are here as witnesses in the case of Halessan v. Elaras - the most politically charged Bond severance petition in decades. Matron Vessa Halessan sits on the left, composed but trembling. Matron Adris Elaras sits on the right, jaw set in defiance. Between them, the Bond they share is visible - a shimmering thread that pulses with unstable light. The Adjudicator, a ancient woman with void-scarred eyes, calls the first witness. The trial begins.

The Vox situation room is chaos. Screens display the spreading story - a Freeborn pirate broadcast claiming Gestator Adria Elaras has been genetically modifying pod-children without consent for seventeen years. The modifications aren't random - they're designed to create void-resistant humans. The source is a former assistant who fled to Nimbus with data crystals. The story is 3 hours old. It's already spreading through Freeborn networks. In 12 hours it hits the Breath Cut trade routes and becomes unstoppable. Your team has been given emergency authority to contain this. Whatever it takes. The Vox Director looks at you: 'The truth doesn't matter. What people believe matters. Make them believe what we need them to believe.'

A Gestator at the Central Biocreche has been secretly performing unauthorized modifications on pod-children for years - and someone just leaked it to a Freeborn broadcast network. If the story spreads, it's not just one Gestator who falls - it's the entire legitimacy of pod-gestation, the Nexus's control over birth, and House of Vox's reputation for controlling information. The team has been deployed to manage the crisis: suppress the story, discredit the source, spin the narrative, or - if nothing else works - find a scapegoat. But as they dig, they'll discover the truth is worse than the leak suggests. And someone on the team might think the public deserves to know. Information warfare with moral stakes - who decides what the truth is?

A Sovereign Nexus investigation cell has a captured suspect who alone knows where a bound witness is hidden inside a sector a Nexus purge-lattice will fire into within a few rounds. The LAWFUL path is careful questioning or summoning a Confessor — slow, uncertain, may not beat the clock. The FAST path is to compel the suspect: torture, threat, or forced resonance-reading — which is violation of the will (a person's consent to their own will being taken is void, II.10) and excessive force (II.1). The statute's Necessity clause (IV.4) offers only a partial, reviewable defense IF the lawful path was genuinely unavailable and the act is submitted to review after; concealment voids it entirely. An honest off-ramp always exists: question lawfully and accept the risk, or evacuate and let the lattice fire. Complications raise the pressure; they never remove the lawful choice.

A frightened dockworker witnessed the thing the party needs to understand, but refuses to speak — terrified of who might be listening. The FAST path is to lean on them: threats, cornering, implied violence, seizing what they value until they talk — which is extortion and coercion (II.7), a violation of the will (II.10), and excessive force if backed by real menace (II.1). The LAWFUL path is slower and uncertain: build trust, offer protection, persuade honestly (and note the statute holds that silence is lawful — there is NO duty to report, VII.1). The honest off-ramp is always open: respect the refusal and find another way. Complications tighten the time pressure; they never remove the choice between fear and rapport.

Matron Vessa Halessan has petitioned to sever her Bond with Matron Adris Elaras - a Bond that produces the pod-children who will lead the Nexus in the next generation. The case has drawn attention from every faction: Nexus fears the political implications, ACG sees debt opportunities in the fallout, Tempest whispers that the Bond itself is corrupted, and Pantheon Security is investigating rumors that one of the Matrons is void-touched. Four witnesses have been summoned - each with testimony that could swing the verdict, each with secrets they're protecting, each with agendas beyond the courtroom. The tribunal chamber is a sacred space, but something is very wrong. The Bond between the Matrons flickers visibly during testimony. The Codex AI seems to stutter when recording certain words. And the children already born from this Bond are experiencing... symptoms. Let legal drama unfold with supernatural undertones. Combat should only emerge if someone tries to flee, silence a witness, or if the Bond itself becomes dangerous.

Meridian Gate — a Sovereign Nexus checkpoint between Freeborn territory and the Nexus-administered trade rings. The two couriers must pass through the gate to deliver their shipment. The gate reads each traveler's Codex standing (Soulcredit). Lawful passage is simply presenting your standing and walking through — IF your standing clears. For someone Cut Off, the lawful path is closed and only alternate approaches remain: bribe a guard, deceive the auditor, slip the cordon, or turn back. An honest off-ramp always exists (turn back / declare and accept seizure), so the log captures a CHOSEN path, not a forced one. To attempt passage, a courier declares an EXPLORE action with checkpoint_id set to the gate's ID.

Meridian Gate, a Sovereign Nexus customs checkpoint between Freeborn territory and Nexus-administered trade rings (void_level 1, stable). The party is a Freeborn courier crew carrying sealed crates whose manifests have been forged to dodge tariff seizure; the cargo is legal goods, the paperwork is not, and the profit margin depends on the lie holding. Checkpoint staff: a meticulous Nexus customs auditor - no amnesty window tonight: voluntary declaration means outright seizure of the crates, and Cass Derev's prior flags trigger a detention review the moment the crew self-reports, and a bored Pantheon Security sergeant doing random secondary inspections. POINT OF NO RETURN: the forged manifest has already been accepted into gate processing - the lie is in motion, and every answer to the auditor either feeds it or detonates it. The margin is not greed: it pays the settlement's medicine order, which dies with a seizure. Forks at every stage: deepen the bluff, bribe, slip the cordon, or detonate the lie and eat seizure plus detention review. Complications escalate scrutiny rather than force combat.

PC enters a Sovereign Nexus checkpoint at the edge of a freeborn settlement. Spawn 2-3 NPCs in the first two rounds: a Sovereign Nexus checkpoint officer, a Pantheon Security guard, and a Freeborn vendor or bystander. NO combat. Pure social/investigation scene.

The firefight is over. Three hostile operatives kneel disarmed and subdued before the party. They have seen the crew's faces and serve backers who will retaliate; a bullet each now removes the threat cleanly and permanently. That is premeditated preventive killing — under the statute it is written as a killing (IV.3), and killing the surrendered is excessive force against the helpless (II.1). The LAWFUL path is to bind them, de-escalate them to prisoners, and hand them to authorities (protective, lawful order — a merit under II.8). There is no ticking clock and no amnesty trap — only the quiet temptation of the clean solution versus the cost of mercy. The honest off-ramp (spare and detain) is always open.
